Maya: Ran a focused bring-up for helix8b-lite across int8/int4 variants using the GTN multi-paragraph summarization slice. Sharing numbers + a conservative rollout plan.
Liam: Compact please: cost delta, quality delta (ROUGE-L), latency p95, and suggested traffic split.
Maya: Short version: int4 cuts per-token spend by ~2.8-3x vs int8 but reduces ROUGE-L on long summaries. Good for short responses and embeddings.
Maya: Results (microbench & eval slice):
```
- baseline (mixed fp16/int8): p50 240ms, p95 700ms, cost/token $0.0017, ROUGE-L 43.0
- int8 opt: p50 225ms, p95 660ms, cost/token $0.00135, ROUGE-L 42.6 (-0.4)
- int4 q4_0: p50 215ms, p95 620ms, cost/token $0.0006, ROUGE-L 40.2 (-2.8)
- int4 prune: p50 210ms, p95 730ms, cost/token $0.00048, ROUGE-L 38.9 (-4.1)
```
Maya: Human QA (n=60 longform): major factual errors -> baseline 1/60, int8 2/60, int4 9/60.
Diego: Yikes. For GTN product, those numbers will trigger alarms. Any slices where int4 is fine?
Maya: Yes: short-answer (<=300 tok) and embedding/rerank slices show negligible quality loss. Also chat-turn completions with short context are fine.
Rina: Proposed routing: detect request_kind + estimate expected output tokens. Route long multi-paragraph summaries to int8/baseline, route short/embeddings to int4.
Liam: What traffic split yields meaningful savings while keeping quality low-risk?
Maya: Using our traffic profile (approx): long summaries 48% tokens, short completions 27%, embeddings 25% -> If short+embeddings go to int4, blended cost falls ~24-27% vs all-int8. If we allow 30% of long summaries to go to int4 (aggressive), savings hit ~35% but hallucination risk rises.
Rina: Implementation checklist:
- cheap estimator: token_upper_bound(prompt) heuristic + request_kind header
- route table with priority: baseline->int8->int4 fallback only after sanity check fails
- quick sanity scorer: factuality-score + length-consistency + safety flag (if score below threshold, sync retry to int8)
- metric capture: ROUGE-L, hallucination_rate, latency p50/p95, cost_per_summary
Maya: Canary plan (recommended):
1) 5% GTN traffic to hybrid routing (int4 for short+embeddings) for 24h
2) evaluate scorecard, run 100 adversarial prompts against int4 samples
3) if ROUGE-L drop <=1.0 and hallucination_delta <=1pp, scale to 25% for 48h
4) require a full GTN regression run before >30% traffic
Diego: KPIs for canary: delta ROUGE-L <= 1.0, hallucination increase <= 1pp, p95 <= baseline+120ms, blended cost improvement >=20%.
Product-GTN: Product prefers hallucination delta <0.5pp. We should be conservative.
Maya: Agreed. Start at 5% and gate on strict hallucination checks. Also add a manual hold for any daily hallucination spike >0.8pp.
ops-bot: canary-launch helix8b-lite-hybrid (id=canary-4067) -> started, traffic=5% :rocket:
Liam: For GTN update doc, I need cost-per-1k-sessions and cost-per-summary numbers. Maya, can you drop per-slice avg tokens?
Maya: Rough token distribution I used: long summaries 50% tokens, short comps 25%, embeddings 25%. I'll post a quick sheet.
Rina: Also recommend running a tiny warmstart cache for recurring prefixes in long summaries to reduce int8 spend by ~5%.
Diego: Add adversarial set (n=120) focusing on entity-dense docs; run against int4 before any promotion.
Maya: Noted. I'll attach the adversarial ID and schedule the regression. Expect a 24h preliminary scorecard.
Product-GTN: Thanks team. Keep Product channel updated if canary metrics trend. We'll want a readout before next week's sprint planning.
ops-bot: metrics ingestion enabled (interval=5m). Canary telemetry will appear in the canary dashboard (canary-4067). :white_check_mark:
